title: Directional Triads in Postpositions: Stationary vs Motion

sections.content:
You know the three-way contrast of the case endings (*-ban*, *-ba*, *-ból*: where, where to, where from). Postpositions with a personal ending have it too:
- **Stationary (Where? Hol?):** *mellettem* (beside me), *előttem* (in front of me), *mögöttem* (behind me)
- **Motion towards (Whither? Hová?):** **mellém** (to my side), **elém** (in front of me / to meet me), **mögém** (behind me)
- **Motion away (Whence? Honnan?):** **mellőlem** (from my side), **előlem** (from before me), **mögülem** (from behind me)

Note: *után* (after) has no such triad; *utánam* ("after me, following me") is a plain inflected form, as in *Gyere utánam!*

items.spanish: Gyere utánam a forgalmas utcán, mutatom az utat!
items.english: Follow me on the busy street, I'll show the way!

items.spanish: Ülj le mellém a padra, pihenjünk egy kicsit!
items.english: Sit down beside me on the bench, let's rest a bit!

items.spanish: A barátom elém jött az állomásra virággal.
items.english: My friend came to meet me at the station with flowers.
